key_insight: AI-based spatial profiling linked elevated tumor MET expression to immune exclusion in head and neck cancer, with distinct patterns in Black/African American patients.
clinical_relevance: Higher predicted spatial MET expression was associated with better response and outcomes on pembrolizumab plus cabozantinib, suggesting a potential biomarker for further study.
method: Deep learning-based spatial profiling of the tumor immune landscape
Comparison of MET expression and immune features across racial groups
Evaluation across independent cohorts and a phase 2 combination-treatment cohort
evidence_signal: Across independent cohorts, higher MET expression correlated with reduced CD8 T-cell infiltration; in the phase 2 cohort, its association with treatment benefit was particularly pronounced among Black/African American patients.
watch_item: These associations do not establish causality or a validated treatment-selection biomarker; cohort sizes and predictive performance are not reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Spatial Profiling Identifies MET-Associated Immune Exclusion and Therapeutic Vulnerability Underlying Racial Disparities in Head and Neck Cancer
